title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Ch. 12: Macalintal v. Comelec — Absentee Voting
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Chapter 12: CJP on Macalintal v. Comelec, upholding the constitutionality of overseas absentee voting under RA 9189
sub_topics: Constitutional qualifications for suffrage (Art. V) — citizenship, age, residence
Congress's mandate to provide a system for absentee voting by Filipinos abroad
Macalintal's challenge to RA 9189 (Overseas Absentee Voting Act)
The Court's ruling upholding absentee voting as constitutional
signature_phrases: a system for absentee voting by qualified Filipinos abroad

stances.claim: Overseas absentee voting is constitutional; the residence requirement does not bar qualified Filipinos abroad from the suffrage Congress was mandated to enable.

notable_anecdotes: The Constitution itself directs Congress to provide for absentee voting by qualified Filipinos abroad.
decision_framework_signals: harmonize residence requirement with the absentee-voting mandate
one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 12 examines Macalintal v. Comelec, which upheld the constitutionality of the Overseas Absentee Voting Act (RA 9189). CJP explains how the Court reconciled the constitutional residence requirement for suffrage (Art. V) with Congress's express mandate to provide a system of absentee voting for qualified Filipinos abroad.
